NEWS 2026-11-19 IBTimes India ('India is playing a whole new game': PM Modi shares GTA VI-themed post highlighting countr):
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday shared a post inspired by the popular video game Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI), highlighting India's transformation across several sectors and comparing the country's progress between the releases of GTA V and GTA VI.
Taking to the social media platform X, the Prime Minister shared a series of slides showcasing India's achievements over the years, accompanied by the message, "India is playing a whole new game."
The first slide highlighted India's economic transformation, contrasting its earlier position among the 'Fragile Five' economies with its current status as the world's fastest-growing major economy.
The second slide highlighted a reduction of 27 per cent in extreme poverty, while the third showcased progress of the Swachh Bharat Mission, with sanitation coverage increasing from 39 per cent to 100 per cent.
Another slide highlighted India's growth in renewable energy, showing an increase in solar power capacity from 2.82 GW to 175 GW.
The Prime Minister also highlighted the growth of India's space startup ecosystem, which expanded from just one startup to 440. Another slide showcased the country's electrification progress, with coverage rising from 20 per cent to 99.6 per cent.
Highlighting the country's digital transformation, PM Modi shared that internet prices had dropped significantly, from Rs 308 per GB to just Rs 7.51 per GB.
The post also showcased India's changing position in the global defence market, from being a major defence importer to exporting defence equipment to more than 80 countries.
In the final slide, the Prime Minister highlighted the reduction in Naxal-affected districts, from 182 to zero.
Meanwhile, GTA VI, developed by 'Rockstar Games', has generated considerable excitement among gaming enthusiasts. The latest instalment takes players back to Vice City and other locations in the fictional state of Leonida, featuring protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who find themselves caught in a crime-filled world.
New Zealand was among the first countries where players could access the game, with internet service providers preparing for a surge in downloads as midnight approached.
For millions of gaming enthusiasts, the release marks a major moment after years of anticipation.

Political leaders and top consumer brands across India are swiftly hijacking the cultural launch of a blockbuster video game to drive viral marketing campaigns and political messaging. Quick-commerce apps are seeing massive surges in physical game sales alongside corporate-backed staff holidays. Discover how federal agencies are leveraging the viral aesthetic to target illicit drug networks.

SOURCE theweek.in (GTA 6 meets 'Namma Benglooru': How India’s tech capital built ...):
Indian gamers are thrilled by the arrival of Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI, but many don’t realise how much of the video game was built in India. The world-famous GTA series actually has a long connection with the Indian city of Bengaluru.
According to reports, around 1,615 developers at Rockstar Games’ Bengaluru studio contributed to the making of GTA VI (GTA 6). The team reportedly worked on the game’s environments, assets, and world-building. They helped develop Vice Beach, a location in the game's fictional US state of Leonida.
The Bengaluru team has also worked on GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 in the past.
Another interesting plot point in the story is that one of India’s earliest gaming studios was acquired by the game’s developer in 2019. The Bengaluru-based gaming company called Dhruva Interactive was founded in 1997 by Rajesh Rao.
Rao started the gaming company with one computer and then proceeded to work on major titles for international publishers, including Microsoft, Sony, Disney and Electronic Arts. Rockstar Games acquired the company 22 years later for a deal valued at ₹7.9 million. This absorbed team became part of the Whitefield, Bengaluru studio that worked on GTA VI.
Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi highlighted the city’s contribution to the game, saying, “We all know Bengaluru for its IT industry, but it's exciting to discover the many facets of our ecosystem.”
The viral 'Namma Benglooru'
While Indian GTA VI fans cheer for the Bengaluru developers, another one of the city’s homegrown gaming creations is going viral.
If GTA VI is taking you through Vice City, this game brings Bengaluru to the screen. The unreleased game features the city’s distinct environment, complete with traffic jams, potholes, autorickshaws and local characters.
The game follows the life of Arjun, a delivery executive, as he faces challenges and different hurdles.
The gamer can undertake a mission, ride different kinds of vehicles while exploring a virtual version of the Bengaluru city. The game’s website says a free demo session of the game will include 12 missions, 18 vehicle types, street races, odd jobs, police pursuits, and live local weather.
More than 4 lakh players signed up for the demo in the first month. However, the release date for the game has not been announced yet.

What Bengaluru’s GTA 6 contribution means for India’s gaming industry
The reported involvement of more than 1,600 developers from Bengaluru is significant because it points to the scale of work Indian teams can undertake within major international game-development projects.
For years, Indian studios have contributed to global titles through areas such as art production, environment design, asset creation and co-development. Rockstar’s acquisition of Dhruva Interactive in 2019 also illustrates how an Indian studio’s capabilities became part of a major international gaming company.

India’s participation in GTA 6 demonstrates its growing role in the global development ecosystem, but it does not by itself establish that Indian companies are creating or controlling comparable global intellectual property.

India's game developers helped build Grand Theft Auto VI. Now they want to create hits of their own
Rockstar Games' Bengaluru studio helped develop Grand Theft Auto VI, putting the spotlight on India's growing gaming industry. Experts tell CNA that while the country has skilled developers, funding constraints and limited experience in creating commercially successful games remain key hurdles.
BENGALURU: So eager was 26-year-old gaming streamer Deepak Barpa to play Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) that he spent around 8,200 Indian rupees (US$88) to pre-order the game months before he even owned a console.
He even waited anxiously at a Delhi warehouse around 5am for two delivery trucks to be unloaded, hoping one carried his PlayStation 5 (PS5).
The PS5 is among the few consoles on which GTA VI will be available to download.
With his console finally in hand, Barpa is eagerly counting down to Thursday (Nov 19), when American gaming company Rockstar Games is set to release GTA VI, more than 13 years after its predecessor was launched.
He has taken several days off from his job as an operations analyst to play the game at launch and stream it for his followers. “I don't want to miss a single second away from the game,” he told CNA.
The highly anticipated game also has an Indian connection, with developer Rockstar Games' Bengaluru studio contributing to its creation alongside teams worldwide.
In a LinkedIn post, Rockstar India’s studio director Daniel Smith said he was “incredibly proud to be a part of this amazing project”. However, the company has not disclosed which parts of the game were developed in India.
“Global investors no longer have to be convinced that India has the talent. Rockstar India alone is reported to have more developers on GTA VI than any other Rockstar studio. But a skilled team and a hit-making company are different things,” said Anuj Tandon, global partner for emerging markets at gaming-focused venture capital firm Bitkraft Ventures.
The launch highlights India's growing role in global game development, but can its studios create blockbuster franchises of their own?
FROM RACETRACKS TO GLOBAL GAMING HITS
Long before GTA VI, Indian developers were helping create various elements of some of the world's biggest video games.
Among the pioneers was Bengaluru-based Dhruva Interactive, founded by Rajesh Rao in 1997, which contributed to Microsoft's Forza Motorsport franchise and other big-budget titles, commonly known as AAA games.
“We did entire cars for Forza,” Rao recalled, adding that his team also worked on racetracks, environments and characters for several major console games.
By 2016-17, Dhruva was building entire game levels from rough layouts supplied by international clients, taking on a larger role in a process known as co-development.
Rao said Dhruva's expertise attracted Rockstar Games, which acquired the company from Swedish gaming firm Starbreeze in 2019 for US$7.9 million, according to the latter's financial disclosures.
“They were buying the company for the talent and nothing else,” Rao told CNA, referring to Dhruva's experienced artists, level designers and content creators.
Other global gaming companies have also tapped Indian expertise.
Indian developers also contributed to art, animation, programming and design for gaming giant Ubisoft's Assassin's Creed Nexus virtual reality edition, the company's Mumbai production director Sashi Menon said in a 2023 interview.

The story of Dhruva Interactive: Predecessor of Rockstar India
Before it became part of Rockstar India, many in the team were working with Dhruva Interactive, India's oldest game development studio.
In May 2019, Rockstar acquired Dhruva Interactive from Swedish publisher Starbreeze for about $7.9 million. Dhruva was then integrated into Rockstar India.
Rajesh Rao, the studio's founder, started a one-person multimedia business from home in Bengaluru in 1995 with a single computer and a dial-up modem, bought with seed money from his father and a bank loan. It shifted into game development in 1997, when Rao formally founded Dhruva Interactive, and became one of India's earliest dedicated game studios.
When Rockstar acquired Dhruva, it had roughly 300 employees specialising in art, level design and other production work. Many continued on projects during the transition, with Rao advising in the process.
Dhruva was involved in Microsoft's Forza Motorsport series, having built entire cars, racetracks and environments. It also contributed to some AAA titles, having worked on Halo 5, Sea of Thieves and Days Gone, among others.
